messages:
Elaine (AE): quick sync — david from Acme wants final POC scoping for the NLU assistant. can we confirm throughput + budget assumptions?
David (Customer): thanks — yes. goal is a 3-week POC. main success criteria: 1) <250ms p50 for short chat, 2) 99th <800ms, 3) intent classification >= 92% on our eval set. budget: ~$8k for the POC (incl infra).
Linda (SE): noted. can you share expected concurrent users and request patterns? that drives batch sizing.
David (Customer): expected ramp: week1 50 concurrent, week2 200, week3 500 concurrent peaks. typical session = 6 requests, median prompt 90 tokens, completion ~160 tokens.
Omar (SRE): rough qps calc — for 500 concurrent with 6 requests/session and avg think-time ~30s => approx 100 qps peak.
Michael (Solutions): agree with Omar. here's a quick sizing sketch:
```
peak_qps = 100
avg_total_tokens_per_request = 90 + 160 = 250 tokens
tokens_per_sec = peak_qps * 250 = 25,000 tps
if using batch size ~8 and model throughput ~50k tokens/sec/GPU (quantized MPT-like) => need 1 GPU for throughput headroom; for stricter latency need 2 smaller GPUs or 1 high-memory GPU with lower latency profile.
```
Raj (Finance): POC budget $8k — how does that map to hours? e.g., if a p4d-ish node is $32/hr, 1 node for 72 hours = $2304. want an itemized estimate.
Linda (SE): itemized estimate (rough):
- infra (dedicated GPU instances, incl networking): 1x high-perf GPU for 3 weeks of intermittent test + 2 smaller GPUs for peak run = ~ $4,200
- data transfer & storage (logs, evals): $300
- Redwood managed service + support hours: $2,500
- contingency (extra run time, debug): $1,000
=> total ~ $8,000 (aligns with customer ask).
Omar (SRE): latency risk callout — batching helps cost but increases p99. if we need p50<250ms, we should set max_batch_delay=3ms and prefer lower batch sizes during interactive traffic. fallback policy: single-token streaming and model-lower-latency variant.
David (Customer): can you note model options? we prefer open models. accuracy on our eval set matters more than tiny latency wins.
Michael (Solutions): propose two-arm POC:
- Arm A (accuracy-first): Llama2-70B-ggml optimized (higher tokens/GPU but higher mem) — target quality.
- Arm B (latency-first): 13B quantized variant with aggressive kernel optimizations.
We run A/B on a 10k prompt eval set and track classification F1 and response latency.
Elaine (AE): success criteria to record in SOW: 1) classification F1 >= 0.92 on eval; 2) p50 latency <= 250ms for 80% of interactive traffic; 3) end-to-end infra cost for the POC <= $8k.
sec-bot: security checklist reminder: need SOC2 attestation excerpt, customer IP whitelisting, and mention of KMS for key handling. share security questionnaire answers by EOD Friday.
Linda (SE): action items: 1) I'll produce a 1-page runbook for traffic ramp + batch settings. 2) Michael will prepare eval harness and prompt set ingestion. 3) Omar will draft the instance specs and fallback routing.
David (Customer): thanks, team. timeline check — can we start week of next Monday? need smoke test in 48 hours of deploy.
Elaine (AE): yes — target kickoff next Monday. I'll circulate SOW draft today and tag the security answers.
Raj (Finance): I'll provision a temporary spend cap in billing portal for the $8k POC. ping me if we need to expand. :thumbsup:
Omar (SRE): one more note — add KV prefix caching for common prompts, that can cut tokens ~12% in our initial sims. will include in runbook.
Michael (Solutions): adding A/B test metrics to the dashboard: per-model F1, per-model p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1000-requests.
Elaine (AE): perfect. closing loop: I'll update the channel with the SOW link + kickoff invite. thanks all. :rocket:
